column1: # What the exit daemon (exitd) and the route helper (exitd_route) need from the policy and from their init definition, one row
# per operation, read from straces of the real binary on `lynx` image 2026102303 (2026-10-29): startup, Tor bootstrap with a
# Tor class in the table (`exitd: bootstrapped`), and a route apply and clear that left the kernel as it found it. Checked by
# check-syscall-policy.py against a compiled policy and exit.rc, so that a missing rule, xperm number or group is found
# before an image is built, not by a service that dies after the first failed call (NET-009: three images, one defect each).
# Columns (tab separated): kind, source, target, class, permissions or numbers, need, evidence
#   kind  allow      every permission is granted to the source on the target (`self` is the source itself)
#         allowxperm every number (ioctl or nlmsg, hex, ranges as a-b) is granted for the named permission
#         deny       none of the permissions may be granted (the design says the helper has no inet socket)
#         gid        the service in exit.rc lists the group (columns: kind, service, group name, -, -, need, evidence)
#   need  required   the row fails the check
#         optional   a denial is tolerated: the daemon was run with the read failing (strace -e inject=openat:error=EACCES)
#                    and kept running; the denial shows in the log and the row records that nothing depends on it
